cryptographic open individual export licences (oiels) will be discontinued following a detailed review of some of our licence types, ecju has decided to phase out the cryptographic oiel and will stop issuing any new cryptographic oiels from 1 december 2026. exporters wishing to export goods or technology incorporating cryptographic functions will instead need to apply for a military or dual-use oiel, as appropriate. applicants who have a live cryptographic oiel application in spire which has not yet been finalised have been notified directly about the transitional arrangements. existing extant cryptographic oiel licences which have already been issued are not impacted by this change, remain valid and may continue to be used. 2. information to include in future oiel applications ecju requires more information on future military and dual-use oiel applications to allow advisers to fully assess each application. when applying for a military or dual-use oiel, rather than providing individual line items, applicants will need to provide a category of items together with an explanation. 2.1 example an example of the level of information that may be required is: equipment specially designed for information security and designed or modified to use cryptography employing digital techniques to perform cryptographic functions, excluding cryptanalysis, as follows: access
